text:
Lena Ortiz: Heads-up: customer asks for a simplified onprem packaging path focused on minimal-network assumptions. proposing a small "lite" flow: offline bundle + explicit preflight network validator. Thoughts?
Marco Diaz: Love the lite flow. we should define what "minimal-network" means: management plane only (TCP 443 + 9411) and optional data-plane peering. document both.
Priya Rao: Acceptance criteria idea for lite packaging:
- installer can run without outbound DNS (all assets from local registry)
- preflight fails fast with clear remediation steps
- docs include sample firewall rules and NAT preservation guidance
DevSec Bot: security checklist: signed bundles, policy for external certs, minimum tls/cipher list, and audit-log toggle for airgapped installs.
Will Turner: Ops note: include a small connectivity-check tool that verifies port reachability, DNS override file presence, and time sync. two-line usage: `redwood-preflight --check-ports --check-registry`.
Lena Ortiz: What about upgrades in lite mode? I propose we only support manual upgrades for v1 and require a preflight re-run before changing images. auto-upgrade is later.
Marco Diaz: Agreed. Also add kernel checks (4.14+), and call-out that Windows nodes are not supported in this path initially.
Priya Rao: Action items:
- Marco: draft preflight validator + firewall doc (due Tue)
- Will: stub the preflight CLI and usage text (due Tue)
- Lena: write lite-packaging acceptance criteria and add to roadmap board (due Wed)
DevSec Bot: policy note logged: airgap-bundle must include cosign signature and package provenance metadata.
Will Turner: I'll post a tiny example for NAT preservation in the doc.
Lena Ortiz: Thanks, keeping thread for the PM sync. we'll reference this in the pilot checklist.
